visual.general_description: Single grayscale axial non-contrast head CT slice of the brain in brain window; no panel letters, side markers, arrows or text.
visual.detailed_description: Grayscale axial CT slice at about the level of the lateral ventricles on a black background. A bright white ring of skull encloses gray brain parenchyma with the interhemispheric fissure at the midline anteriorly and a thin bright midline line posteriorly. The two lateral ventricles are dark, symmetric-looking CSF-density spaces flanking the midline, and cortical sulci are visibly widened over both hemispheres. On the image-right side a lateral frontoparietal zone looks lower in density with wider dark sulcal spaces than the opposite side. A thin soft-tissue scalp layer surrounds the skull and is thicker and irregular along the image-left side. Curved bright lines at the bottom of the image are the head holder/table. No text, laterality letters, scale bar, arrows or annotations are visible.

visual.general_description: Single grayscale axial brain MRI slice with bright CSF in widened sulci; no panel letters, side markers, arrows or text.
visual.detailed_description: Grayscale axial MRI slice through the upper cerebral hemispheres on a black background. The brain is enclosed by a dark skull/scalp rim with a gray subcutaneous layer. Cortical sulci are widened over both hemispheres and filled with bright CSF signal, outlining gyri that are intermediate to dark gray, with white matter darker gray. The interhemispheric fissure is a thin bright vertical line at the midline. Ill-defined brighter patches lie in the deep white matter on both sides of the midline in the central/posterior part of the slice. Lateral ventricles are not conspicuous at this level. No text, laterality letters, sequence label, scale bar, arrows or annotations are visible.

imaging_submodalities.visual_cue: CSF in sulci is bright relative to darker white matter, an appearance like a T2-weighted sequence; sequence is not labelled
